name: @circle-fin/daa-web-sdk
//private: Stays true in the repo. The release workflows flip it to false in the manifest they pack, so nothing can be published by accident from a checkout or a stray `pnpm publish`.
description: Browser SDK for Digital Asset Accounts — Strong Customer Authentication passkey ceremonies
//engines: An install- and integration-time claim, not a runtime one: this package runs in a browser and has no Node runtime requirement of its own. It says Circle supports installing and bundling this with a Node 22+ toolchain — and that is enforceable rather than advisory, so a consumer running engine-strict=true on an older toolchain has the install refused (measured on npm 11.16.0: EBADENGINE, exit 1). Declared anyway, with that cost understood: one floor across both halves of the same SDK is clearer to an integrator than one half declaring nothing. Kept identical to packages/node; if the two ever need to differ, that is worth a sentence here rather than a silent drift.
